data.name: Ekagrah
data.gender_notes: Ekagrah is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Ekagrah is derived from the Sanskrit word 'eka' meaning one and 'agrah' meaning point or focus. It represents a person with a single-minded focus or intense concentration. In Hindu mythology, Ekagrah is also associated with Lord Shiva, who is known for his unwavering focus and intense devotion. The name Ekagrah carries the meaning “One-pointed mind” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ekagrah usually hope their child will grow to embody one-pointed mind and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes inner peace and focus, a clear mind devoted to a single purpose.
data.etymology: Ekagrah belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “One-pointed mind.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ekagrah total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

historical_references.reference: In Hindu mythology, Ekagrah is the name of a powerful demon who was vanquished by Lord Shiva. Ekagrah was born from the mind of the demon Tripura, and was characterized by his single-minded focus and determination to destroy Lord Shiva. He is often depicted as having only one eye, representing his unwavering focus on his goal.

Ekagrah is also mentioned in the Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic, as the name of a powerful yogi who attained the ability to see the past, present, and future. He was able to do this through intense meditation and focus, symbolized by the name Ekagrah (one-pointed).

YouTube is a popular platform for discovering and learning various forms of meditation and mindfulness practices, including those that aim to cultivate the state of Ekagrah. Instagram, with its visual focus and large community, is also a platform where individuals can share their meditation and mindfulness practices, creating a supportive and engaging network. The Apple App Store is home to a multitude of meditation and mindfulness apps, many of which offer guided practices and tools designed to help individuals cultivate the state of Ekagrah.
